extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers, JIC staff, IMT members, and emergency/incident communication planners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for operating a Joint Information Center (JIC) and developing communications strategy during incidents (particularly wildland fire). Covers coordination, staffing, facilities, web/information management, tactical implementation, and message planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with MAC, IMT, South Ops, and statutory agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Close coordination with MAC Group, IMT's, South Operations, and statutory agencies is essential to successfully provide accurate and timely information to elected officials and agency leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The JIC manager or JIC political/elected Lead will establish communication channels with these and other appropriate agencies to coordinate briefings or responses to issues. RECOMMENDATION: Establish a liaison person at JIC to work directly with South Ops. Establish an information person with the IMT to be directly at the incident to convey information to JIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and maintain elected-officials contact list
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a key contact list with names, telephone numbers, e-mails, addresses of all town, city, county elected officials along with state representatives and congressional representatives in the MAST area of influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish MAST agency headquarter offices addresses and key contacts for forwarding information regarding incident developments or unique situations regarding elected official contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIC facilities and phone system standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately develop JIC workstations for a minimum number of people and establish primary and unpublished phone lines and rollover systems for public lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RECOMMENDATION examples: develop JIC workstations for a minimum of three people (or other section-specific minimums), establish a primary phone line, rollover phone system for the public lines, and two unpublished lines; develop a JIC masthead for news releases and correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaster Services and Law Enforcement section functions
rubrics_metrics.description: This section supports IMTs, statutory evacuation/road management agencies, public service agencies to provide information regarding evacuations, damage assessment teams, casualty teams, and public services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary responsibilities: (1) Clearinghouse - serves as a clearinghouse for information flows using information received from statutory information officers or directors. (2) Web Information - provide cleared/approved information to the JIC web manager for posting on the website. Information is gathered and disseminated using approved incident updates from delegated or statutory units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum staffing composition and scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum staffing upon activation includes representatives from federal (USFS), state (CDF), county fire, county sheriff, CalTrans, CHP, County OES, utilities (e.g., Southern California Edison), and Red Cross; a minimum staff count is specified for 24-hour shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: A minimum staff should consist of 10 information officers through a 24-hour shift (Disaster Services/LE). Media relations sometimes specifies a full minimum staff of 6 information officers through a 24-hour period and elsewhere 10; IMT determines expansion. Staffing recommendations include having a lead officer qualified to Type 1 with extensive wildland fire experience and ideally structure loss/evacuation experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead officer qualifications and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead officer (manager) ensures accurate and approved information is coordinated with the IMT Information Officer (or designated staff), statutory agencies and the damage assessment team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead should be a qualified Incident Information Officer equal to a Type 1 qualification with extensive wild land fire experience and ideally with structure loss or evacuation experience. Roles include preparing fact sheets, coordinating clearinghouse, assigning info officer to damage assessment team, ensuring evacuation/road status info flow, obtaining subject-matter consultants (e.g., animal damage), coordinating news conference needs, and developing mass trauma response plans with MAC/IMT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and use fact sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare fact sheets for public dissemination and use frequently to share information with all JIC sections to ensure accuracy and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either the JIC manager or a MAC Group representative should review public release of information. RECOMMENDATION: Establish a template for the fact sheets listing responsive agencies and a JIC masthead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web management responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Web section develops a JIC web page to aggregate information received from an IMT and other sources and links the page to local, county, state, and federal agencies or organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary responsibilities: (1) Clearinghouse - maintain and update information to provide a centralized and consistent information source (information posted must be approved by statutory authorities); (2) Links - establish links with cooperators and partners; (3) Reference Material - create background/reference material and post upon approval of the IMT Information Officer. Staffing: initial minimum of two webmasters; webmasters maintain site 24/7. Designate a web-savvy information officer; obtain a server and web-based equipment immediately ensuring electronic linkage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal section responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure information is shared with JIC agency employees and incident or established partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary responsibilities: (1) Agency Information - provide directors, line officers, agency information officers and cooperators with regular, timely and accurate status reports reviewed by Center Manager; (2) Partner Information - provide status reports to partners (e.g., fire safe councils, rural fire departments); (3) Documentation - establish a documentation section and prepare daily records; (4) Dedicated Liaisons - establish dedicated staff to interact with County OES-EOC and South Ops. Provide timely (minimum of two per day) updates to MAST partners and incident cooperators' home units; develop and utilize e-mail and fax for transmission; establish documentation procedures for entire JIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document protocols and pre-identify staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Section Lead Information Officer will develop protocols and document daily coordination activities and key contacts at all levels for their section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide in advance which agency should lead information during initial attack. The MAC Group, MAST PR Team and Forest PAO should recommend/select JIC Center Manager(s) and Section Leaders immediately. Pre-identifying Section Leads enables staffing identification prior to activation. Strongly consider activating the JIC at the same time a Type 1 or 2 IMT is ordered. Develop an MOU to document MAC Group operation and oversight of the JIC and a separate financial agreement. Consider drills/training to verify and correct precepts of the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for rapid JIC activation timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the primary goals is to have the JIC activated within 6 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interim JIC Manager and Section Leads have been pre-identified, they will be ordered at the same time as the IMT. Bring in resources to implement next phase of JIC development — e.g., team of four to six information officers to help accomplish tactical tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community functional recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish community contact and information distribution mechanisms to feed the JIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish ASAP through Fire Safe Councils a phone tree contact list or other mailing lists for direct information feeds; use this as a reference guide at the JIC; develop a Desk Guide on community key contacts; immediately develop JIC workstations for minimum staffing (examples: 8 personnel) and phone configuration (primary, unpublished, rolling ring for public number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations functional recommendations and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a media section capable of handling media needs and replicate media center capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum staffing includes federal/state/county fire and sheriff representatives; full minimum staff examples: 6 information officers through 24-hour shifts and/or 10 personnel workstations. Publicize JIC telephone number and likely staffing schedule. Prepare desk guides of media contacts. Equip media section with televisions with recorders, cable service, radio scanners, fax machines, telephones, erase boards, computers/printers and office supplies; order podium/lectern with working surface and light.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political/elected officials handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate staffing and processes to handle elected officials' information needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum staffing: information specialist and agency representatives; MAC Group makes immediate decision on a JIC leader. Develop a key contact list for town/city/county/state/congressional representatives. Establish MAST agency headquarters addresses and key contacts for forwarding information regarding incident developments. Develop JIC masthead for news releases and correspondence. Provide minimum of three-person workstations and phone rollover arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turn-key operational tactics: parking
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify parking system needs at the JIC building for satellite trucks, working staff, media, and visitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactical item to be implemented immediately to get JIC operational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephones and radios configuration and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational telephone and radio setup standards for the JIC communications flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Walk-around telephones with lights and turn off ringers; there will be no 1-800 number for JIC (existing 1-800 may remain elsewhere); rollover existing USFS and SB Co fire media and public numbers to the JIC or obtain and publish JIC numbers if not possible; public phone goes to Community Section and will roll over internally; specify counts for lines (e.g., 11 public lines available, 15 optimum; media lines eight incoming and two reserved for outgoing). All JIC sections with direct phone lines should have voicemail capability for after-hours or busy times. Have four programmable scanners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment and physical supplies list
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventory and procure essential physical equipment and supplies for JIC operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested items: 2 fax machines incoming and 2 outgoing (4 total?), multiple white dry erase boards, chairs (e.g., 48 desks and 120 meeting chairs), flipchart/easel/whiteboard combo, 80-120 folding chairs, large lectern, TVs (several), one power point projector with screen, risers for media briefing and TV cameras, heavy-duty color and b/w copiers, refrigerator and microwave, portable ice chests, ice machine, plain wall clocks, large map board with sticky capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel roles and tactical staffing needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and assign tactical roles required to sustain JIC operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify a minimum of two 'runners' to update info boards; create a rollout/push list identifying O-numbers by agency; establish dispatch or tone-out to call out JIC staffers; consider identifying a satellite coordinator; identify administration support needs and team members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer, network, and software requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure computing resources and software compatibility for JIC operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure Internet access available at all workstations. Need examples: 48 desktop computers and three b/w and one-color printer; check server needs and interagency compatibility; check WINFAX compatibility; have business card software and preset business card sheets ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of a communications strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: A communications strategy should include essential named elements to structure outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements listed: Introduction (summarize the incident); Communication goals and objectives; Target audiences; Key messages and talking points; Communication methods (how are you getting your message out? e.g., trapline, radio, congressional briefing); Action items, assignments, and timelines (Who? What? When? Where? Why?). Could be as short as one page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication goals vs objectives and outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish broad goals from specific measurable objectives to give direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without clear and specific outcome measures, communication can lack direction and effect. Goals are broad statements describing purpose; objectives are things that lead to accomplishing goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider long-term implications of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that communications policies and actions during an incident may have long-term effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use incidents to serve jurisdictional agency long-term interests (e.g., working with LEPC and first responders). Be alert to opportunities to achieve strategic objectives beyond those directly related to the incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and prioritize target audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically identify audiences to be reached and prioritize messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask local officials which audiences you should speak to; they can identify audiences you might not think of and advise on which media to use (newspapers, newsletters, etc.). Audiences may be broken down as local/internal, external/regional/national, and political.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and pretest key messages (limit to three)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop key messages and talking points, generally limiting to three main messages for Incident Commander delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three is a rule of thumb not absolute—PIO should use judgment. You might write six or so in the plan but do not give the Incident Commander more than three. Develop talking points from key messages. Prioritize information, tailor messages to each audience (children, adults, environmentalists), develop methods (briefing papers, fact sheets, newsletters, news releases, posters, video/radio, internet/social media), specify method and frequency of contact, and be realistic—do not make promises you cannot keep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Message tailoring and audience-specific tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor content and tactics for different audience groups and deliver via appropriate channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of tailoring: for children (avoid contaminated sites, affirm safety), adults (resource protection), environmentalists (species protection). Use different methods for different audiences: briefing papers, fact sheets, newsletters, news releases, posters, video/radio, Internet/web pages and/or social media platforms. Specify method and frequency of contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for external influences (short- and long-term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify external influences that may affect public perception and communication strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External influences with short-term effects and with long-term effects should be considered. Sensitive social, political and economic issues to consider include effects on local economy, active interest from elected officials, interruption of traditional community events, community attitudes toward the agency, historical reactions by community and media, and cultural considerations. Local Agency Administrator/Executive or Public Affairs Officer can aid in assessing these effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for internal influences and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify internal factors that affect communications strategy and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider availability of resources (personnel and equipment), indicators of competition for scarce resources (other incidents, emergency declarations, national readiness), additional resources from local volunteer groups, local agencies' policy considerations (subject matter expert or agency spokesperson), communications philosophy of Agency Administrator, and issues agency does not want a PIO to discuss (e.g., poor security).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor effectiveness of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuously monitor incident operations and media coverage to adjust strategy and maintain situational awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All the way through the process, the PIO needs to monitor incident operations and media coverage and keep his or her 'head up.' Use monitoring to inform adjustments in messaging and tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications plan objectives and delivery (case-specific template)
rubrics_metrics.description: A communications plan should set a release timeline, identify participating parties and roles, inform internal/external audiences, and address issues associated with the report or incident; include an action plan mapping audience → method → content → responsible persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (Sawtooth plan): Goals include releasing the investigation report timely; objectives include developing timeline, listing participants/roles, coordinating release, and identifying resource needs. Primary audiences identified (family, on-site personnel, BIA employees, tribal members); delivery methods include personal briefings, press briefings, agency internet sites, face-to-face meetings, and CD-ROM distribution. Action Plan table matches Target Audience to Communication Method, What to deliver, and Who (e.g., Family of Rick Lupe: Personal Briefing; Report and Findings; Nordwall, Philbin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Key messages for investigation report rollouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft key messages that establish the nature and credibility of the investigation and emphasize priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample key messages from Sawtooth: 'The Sawtooth Mountain Accident Investigation Team is a fact-finding team, not a fault-finding team.'; 'Firefighter and public safety is always the top priority within the Bureau of Indian Affairs.'; Team members selected for qualifications and followed departmental investigation protocols; Team was professional, thorough, objective; The Accident Team established probable events and documented findings to prevent similar occurrences.
